notes.author: Chloe Nakamura
notes.text: Kickoff with Marcus Delgado. Leadership wants to replace the points-based loyalty program with tiered member pricing nationwide in one launch before holiday. Budget $1.1M.

notes.author: Owen Park
notes.text: Priya Raman's team found that 18% of revenue comes from members who only redeem points during clearance. Tiered pricing could alienate them. No way to predict response from historical data alone.

notes.author: Chloe Nakamura
notes.text: Convinced Marcus to test first: 3 matched test regions vs 3 control regions for 8 weeks, with a pre-agreed kill metric (member churn above 4%).

notes.author: Owen Park
notes.text: Test results: tiered pricing lifted member spend 6% but churn among clearance-only members hit 9% in one region. Adjusted design to keep a points track for that segment.

notes.author: Chloe Nakamura
notes.text: Revised hybrid program rolled out nationally. Churn within target. Marcus: "The test saved us from a very public mistake."

simulation.lesson: Before rolling out a major customer-facing pricing or loyalty change everywhere, run a controlled test in matched regions against control regions with a kill metric agreed in advance. Historical data often cannot predict how a specific customer segment will react; a bounded test reveals the at-risk segment early enough to redesign rather than reverse a public launch.
simulation.why: Segment reactions are hard to model; a pre-agreed kill metric turns a risky launch into a reversible experiment.
simulation.conditions: Customer-facing change, heterogeneous customer segments, reputational cost of reversal.
